q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT STUDENT, CLASS FROM COURSES ) T GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(CLASS) >= 5
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT STUDENT, CLASS FROM COURSES ) T GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(CLASS) >= 5
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 groups by CLASS and checks if the count of rows (i.e., students) in each class is >= 5. Q2 first removes duplicates by selecting distinct STUDENT and CLASS, then groups by CLASS and checks if the count of distinct CLASS values is >= 5, which is always true as it's grouping by CLASS itself.
counterexample_dsp: Q1 will return classes with at least 5 students, while Q2 will return all classes since the condition is always true due to the GROUP BY CLASS.
